axes.name: Hook & retention
axes.rationale: The opening is immediately drawn, with a large question, moving grip and entering hand; its physical callback closes the argument. The question is more abstract than the historical road-edge hook, and the long sequence of similarly framed laboratory labels creates a modest middle-act sag.

axes.name: Illustration craft & detail
axes.rationale: The lever has metal highlights, inset detents, screw heads and a shaded mount; glazing, feet contact shadows, fabric bands, trouser folds and face shading give the researcher finish parity with the mechanism. Concrete defects: the blue sleeve ends openly in mid-frame at 101s and 110s rather than connecting to an offscreen body; distant harbor buildings have plain uniform fills and repeated geometry beside substantially richer foreground props.

axes.name: Motion & animation craft
axes.rationale: Consecutive strips show grip travel, an initiating hand that releases, feedback-driven lever change, hinged result-flap movement, the duck/reaction, visible modest body/head movement during the harbor hold, and a final hand-guided lever correction. The gate strip visibly fades its isolated sleeve away instead of completing a physical withdrawal. Collar and final-detent moves are very small at phone scale, while large camera drift remains more salient than much of the secondary performance. These are execution deductions within the brand, not a demand for 3D.

axes.name: Composition & staging
axes.rationale: Both biological cases are separately staged, captions remain in a consistent clear band, and equal catch/breeding-stock requirements span both candidates. The 70.5s shot duplicates STOCK-LINKED RECRUITMENT on adjacent plates, increasing crowding. At 110s stacked plaques cover the upper hand area and largely obscure the small background comparison apparatus. The large blank upper laboratory glazing competes for space with the mechanism.

axes.name: Color & grade
axes.rationale: Ultramarine apparatus, sea-glass glazing, alabaster plates and mango grip/jacket form a coherent laboratory-to-harbor color world. The blue is motivated by water and research equipment; warm quay expansion is an effective change of act. It differs clearly from the sepia/teal/plum historical anchor. Distant roof/facade color blocks are less nuanced than foreground grading.

axes.name: Typography & captions
axes.rationale: Serif plates and monospaced captions are crisp, high contrast and readable in the montage. Rendered text matches the scoped comparison claims; no typo or wrong number found. Repeated all-capital plate styling limits hierarchy, and the duplicate stock-linked labels are unnecessary. The separate credit card is readable at full resolution and held for ten seconds; its single long music-credit line is substantially smaller than the source rows and less comfortable at phone size.

axes.name: Sound design & mix
axes.rationale: Evidence-based assessment, without human listening: current audio report measures -14.36 LUFS, -3.26 dBTP and 6.9 LU LRA, all passing; the event file supplies 38 differentiated motivated contact/texture sounds, and quality_report verifies 21 audible event lifts plus a substantial silence dip. The credited Kevin MacLeod bed and selected voice report support a layered balanced mix. The reports do not establish subjective musical fit, timbral refinement or emotional delivery strongly enough for an excellent/perfect taste score.

axes.name: VO–illustration sync & entertainment
axes.rationale: The rendered sequence follows learned feedback, fixed comparison, constant recruitment, distinct stock-linked case, reversal and shared next-test goals in the narration order. Aligned captions and beat/contact records support timing. The physical grip provides continuity and the duck supplies a modest visual joke. Several explanatory moments remain primarily words on moving plaques, so visual entertainment is competent rather than consistently surprising.

axes.name: Accuracy & sourcing
axes.rationale: Claims and verified findings trace the study, affiliations, simulated mechanisms, scenario-specific outcomes and management context to publisher, author code and NOAA primary sources. The picture explicitly labels simulation and each result versus its own comparison, and the honest turn denies demonstrated management advantage while retaining research value. Main outcome claims still rely on one published study; public code is expressly not a reproduction of Figure 4, preventing a top score for independently corroborated load-bearing results. No factual blocker identified in the supplied verified evidence.

axes.name: Alaska authenticity & cultural respect
axes.rationale: Eastern Bering Sea pollock, the Alaska Fisheries Science Center, NOAA and the North Pacific council make the subject concretely Alaska-relevant. The human role is investigative rather than savior-like; there are no unverified Native words or cultural motifs. The generic harbor row and lack of a recognizable local working-fishery detail limit visual specificity.

axes.name: Writing & post quality
axes.rationale: The post makes the changing biological assumption the hook, explains spawning biomass in plain language, preserves separate comparison baselines, and ends with a substantive catch-versus-breeding-stock question. VO advances the same argument without manufactured numerical stakes. The management limitation and testing language recur several times near the end, making that section somewhat repetitive.

limitations: No human listening or continuous real-time playback occurred. Sound score is explicitly based on measured delivered audio and event/voice reports.
Motion judged from actual consecutive rendered strips; stills were used only for composition, lettering and craft.
The square crop is not an aesthetic panel subject; this card scores only the exact 9:16 master.
Research result validation relies on the current supplied verified findings and primary-source mapping; numerical study outputs were not independently reproduced.
